# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-194-194 (§194)

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, run3/RUNBOOK.md §2, packet.md, units.json, secret-history-glossary.json, and the published 191-193 units (plus its review.md for numbering and format; 189-190 units for Tayang, Kürbesü, Inancha-Bilge, torluγ). known-forms.json and novel-forms.json were used only to check lemmas. No modern translation, no web.

Unit numbers are 1-based (unit 1 = "Qaraγ̇ul-un …", unit 36 = "qor(i)-jan …"), as in the 191-193 review. Edits were made by script; layout (indent 1) kept, `t` untouched, no units split or merged.

Checks that passed with no change: every `t` equals the packet words of its index run (36 units, 251 words, indices 0–250 once each, in order); `ln` is 194 on every unit and `p: true` only on unit 1; no unit has a missing `l`/`i`/`n`; one `words` entry per word (unit 26 "Tajaṅ Qān-(n)u" is one packet word with three morphs, correct); the quotation marks as printed (open at "An-a, close at ese-ü"; open at "Küčütü, close at bi-že"; open at "Inanča-Bilge, close at či"; close at bida") are each matched, and the one supplied opening mark (unit 3) is announced in its note; house renderings (Tayang Qan, Qan/Qahan, Qori-Sübechi, Inancha-Bilge, Kökse'ü-Sabraq, Kürbesü, Jamuqa, "geldings", hodun-(n)ača "more … than there are stars", ese vs ülü, torluγ left untranslated, the Ext B character left as a box) agree with conventions.md and the published parts.

## Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

### Medium (sense, label or lemma wrong)
1. 6 · i · medium · the note says "I have not supplied 'with them', which the Ming leaves out", yet `i` read "if we once join with them". · i → "if we once join together,".
2. 7 · l, n, morph (-kün) · medium · the ending of kikün was labelled "first person plural" in the morph and the note ("an ending of the first person plural that I cannot name"), against the glossary's "future participle -kün, 'shall do'" (ker kikün) for the same form. · morph → "future participle: shall … (the Ming 咱 adds 'we, let us'; uncertain)"; n names -kün as the glossary's future participle; l "we-do" → "we-shall-do".
3. 10 · morph (an-i) · medium · lemma "tere" for the printed an-i; the known entry and the Ming (他每行) carry the oblique stem an. · lemma an, gloss "them (third-person plural oblique stem, inferred)", -i accusative kept.
4. 13 · morph (an-u) · medium · lemma "tere" + -u for the printed an-u; 191-193 and the glossary carry lemma an-u as one morph. · single morph an-u, gloss as in 191-193.
5. 15 · i, n · medium · "Ah, thus does the woman Tayang … speak" — "Ah" has no support (the Ming 又 is "again, moreover") and `i` used the present where `l` ("speaking-has") and the form (-žüġüi, past) are past. · i → "And so the woman Tayang, his heart failing, has spoken these words."; n now says 'And so' carries the Ming 又 and ein 'thus', force a guess.
6. 18 · i, n · medium · `i` made γaruγsan a finite "He has never gone out beyond …" and invented a subject "he" (the note admitted "the subject 'he' is not in the grammar"). γaruγsan and kürügsen are past participles that qualify eme at the end of unit 19; "beyond" also reverses the Mongol (dative γažar-a with ese γaruγsan = not gone out TO the place; compare ese kürügsen in the next unit, and ese γaruγsan in 193 unit 56). · i → "One who has never gone out as far as the place where a heavy woman makes water,"; n now says the participle qualifies eme and no subject is supplied.
7. 19 · i, n · medium · same sentence: "has never come to where …, a woman," left eme dangling as an afterthought. · i → "who has never come to where the calves of the cart-wheel graze, a woman —"; n: eme is the noun both participles qualify.
8. 20 · i · medium · "Tayang, a woman of failing heart" turned the apposition (eme Tajaṅ, in unit 19) into a second clause and added "of"; the sentence ends "Tajaṅ žirüge jadarun ese-ü" = Tayang, heart failing, not?. · i → "Tayang, his heart failing: is it not so?"".
9. 21 · i · medium · "Having said these words, he came" makes Küchülüg arrive in person, which contradicts the note ("the English follows the first [the words come]") and unit 22 (he sends envoys). · i → "These words, once spoken, came; so saying,".
10. 23 · i, n · medium · "called a woman by his own son" supplies an agent ("son") that the Mongol does not have: öġer(i)-jen (Ming (自己)自的行) is "his own self", the patient of the two passives (emečilegden, ügülegdežü). · i → "himself treated as a woman and spoken of so,"; n rewritten (the (i) is Shiratori's; no agent named).
11. 26 · i, n · medium · "the great lord who held the lower rank under Tayang Qan" commits to a past ("held") that medekü (a participle, "one who will manage" in the glossary) does not give, and to a rank sense the Ming 下管的 ("manages below") does not. · i → "Tayang Qan's great lord, who had charge of those below,"; n says doro may as well be a rank and medekü is a participle.
12. 30 · i, n · medium · "if the lady is also a person, would she not, bringing your mother Kürbesü along" made the lady the subject who brings Kürbesü, while the note read qatun as Kürbesü herself; Kürbesü-ji is the object of abčiražü and no subject is stated. · i → "if the lady too is a person, would one not, bringing your mother Kürbesü along, …"; n: qatun may be Kürbesü (189–190 "our Lady") but the bringing has no stated subject.
13. 31 · n, morph (čima) · medium · čima called an "accusative form"; in this part's own glossary the accusative is čima-ji and bare čima is the oblique stem. · n and morph → "oblique stem čima-; the Ming takes it here as an exclamation". Speculation about "the old counsellor … gone or too aged to advise" removed (nothing in the Mongol or Ming says it).
14. 35 · i · medium · `i` opened a second double quotation mark ("Ah! …") although the speech begun at unit 27 ("Inanča-Bilge) is still open and closes at či" in this unit; the note itself says the mark "ends Qori-Sübechi's speech". · opening mark removed.

## Findings refused (with reason)
- Unit 24 maqa rendered "may he not", not the house "perhaps (not)": the l keeps "perhaps" and the note says why (maqa with the optative bu … -tuγai, "may he not"); unit 25 uses "perhaps". Kept.
- Unit 27 sača "alike, equally" (Ming 一般) against the glossary's Sača, a man's name: the Ming here is 一般, not 人名, and the glossary already holds sačaγ̇u "alike (一般)". Kept in the unit; for the glosser to broaden the token sača.
- Unit 18 kündü eme "pregnant woman" and the whole jibe: the note marks it as a reading ("I take it of …", "Colourful and uncertain"); the Ming has only 重.
- Unit 16 qaγāča as a rhetorical question: the note says the Ming has no question particle and gives the statement reading. Kept.
- Unit 27 "Inancha-Bilge Qan … the previous ruler of the Naiman": 189–190 already makes him Tayang's father and gives him Qān; kept.
- Unit 17 "Moṅγol" lemma with ṅ (glossary key Monγol): 191-193 uses Moṅγol in morphs. Kept.
- Unit 35 morph turluγ and unit 36 buruγu with no (or a box) Ming bracket: the Ming is blank / Ext B; house rule is to leave torluγ untranslated and never substitute the character. Kept.
- Unit 32 "Why" (i) against "What" (l) for Jaγun: Ming 甚麽; the note gives both readings. Kept.
- Unit 2 quote marks supplied for the message (opening at Moṅγol-un aγtas) and the message itself: the note says the mark is the drafter's; closing mark at bida" is Shiratori's. Kept.
- Units 8, 9, 22, 24, 29, 33: the plan and speeches are uncertain but each note says so; no label wrong.

## For the glosser / pass 2
- sača (Ming 一般) beside Sača [人名]; ein with Ming 是也; bare čima (嘆聲); -kün as future participle with Ming 咱; tarγu as adjective; an with accusative -i; bidan-dur; qamtudun, qamtudγ̇asu, qaγāča, ese-ü, ötöldeküi, -mu; seküġül- as sekü- + causative.

# Review, pass 2 — secret-history-194-194 (§194)

Reviewer: adversarial pass 2 (fresh read of units.json after pass 1, plus a check of every gloss.json entry against the text). Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, gloss.json, novel-forms.json, known-forms.json, the shared secret-history-glossary.json. No modern translation, no web. Edits by script; `t` untouched; unit numbers 1-based as in pass 1. Checked by script and found clean: every `t` equals its packet words; every morph's bracketed Ming (all morphs of a word together) equals the packet Ming for that word; every gloss.json key is a novel token and every novel token has an entry, with its Ming bracket equal to novel-forms.json; every `__broaden__` key is a token of this part, its value begins with the whole old glossary entry + ' · ', and its new reading occurs here.

## Findings refused (with reason)
- Unit 8 i "they do not shrink away" as a finite clause (the adjective chain qaltaril ügei qataṅgin Monγol could also qualify Monγol): ügei is a predicate "there is not", the note states the doubt about who is joined with whom. Kept.
- Unit 2 i "sent it with this message": awkward, but converbs keleležü ilerün are rendered as the note says; no sense error. Kept.
- Unit 29 "If I had known": the speaker is Qori-Sübechi, the subject is natural English for a subjectless participle; kept.
- gloss `qaγ̇āča` "qaγa — where": the form is flagged "analysis uncertain" and the Ming 那裏行 is quoted; no better analysis from the glossary. Kept. Likewise ebere-/berte-/belžiġel/ölkes/oluṅkin/üdü-: stems inferred from the Ming and marked uncertain. Kept.
- `jan` broadening (omog(i)-, qor(i)-): both occur (units 24, 36) and the old entry is whole; kept as is.
- Moṅγol / Monγol lemma spelling in morphs: as pass 1, follows the published parts. Kept.
